rationale: Verification and stopping record, with no new records. The run's two investigations are complete and consistent. The configuration-recovery question (98ee8dfd5fac4b84915f91ed4b094bcf-question-0) rests on seven receipts: the four single-voter recovery cases with their flag-off controls, the three-voter commit-rule witness (reproduced in four receipts), the durable-snapshot corruption that survives a flag-off restart (three receipts), the authority pair including the repeat in which its premise failed and the revised execution that enforces it, and the two-voter probe showing the node still votes for a healthy peer. The replay-completion question (29e4214f5ee146b393957fa23a33a73d-question-0) rests on nine receipts covering the block, the measured bound, the exact 128-versus-129 delivered-batch boundary, reachability with default settings, and the availability consequence, with every pair reproduced at least twice with identical operands. A consistency check of 54 claims across 14 retained receipts against the observations found no discrepancy, and both knowledge corrections raised by this evidence - tuple-counted batching and the randomized snapshot cadence - are recorded with their affected uses marked and their gaps answered. The remaining limitations are structural to the harness (in-memory transports and stores in one process, no production store, no process-level restart or disk fault, one prefix shape per case) or reachable only through a snapshot-shipping scenario that cannot be built and cited within the remaining allocation, so no further work is initiated.
